qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Albemarle holds premier physical asset stakes (Salar de Atacama brine concession in Chile and a 49% interest in the Greenbushes hard-rock mine in Australia), qualifying as irreplaceable natural resource infrastructure. However, it lacks economic pricing power; prices are set by global commodity spot and index benchmarks. Cyclical supply surges from China and alternative geographies severely depressed realized prices by >80% from 2022 peaks, driving GAAP ROIC negative (-8.9% to -13.7% in 2024, -2.0% in 2025) and failing the 12% multi-cycle threshold (10-year median ROIC ~7.5%). Primary erosion threats include global supply volatility, substitution risks, and Chilean state-majority resource control.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). Albemarle controls premier tier-one lithium assets (Atacama brine, Greenbushes JV), but operates as a structural commodity price-taker lacking pricing power >= inflation across the cycle. Multi-cycle capital efficiency fails the Munger hurdle (10-year median GAAP ROIC ~7.5%, plunging to negative returns in 2024-2025 during the cyclical trough). Extreme earnings volatility, multi-billion-dollar asset write-downs, and emerging Chilean resource nationalism negate sustainable economic rent protection.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is ~7.5%, well below the 12% hurdle. After an unrepeatable peak during the 2022-2023 lithium spike ($70k+/ton), realized lithium prices collapsed to ~$10-$12/kg, resulting in a FY2024 GAAP net loss of $(1.2B) and deeply negative ROIC (-8.9% to -13.7%). CapEx had to be slashed from >$2B to ~$600M in 2025 alongside significant asset impairments, restructuring charges, and bank covenant amendments through mid-2026. While operational cash flow and FCF rebounded in late 2025/2026 as lithium pricing stabilized near $20/kg, Albemarle remains fully exposed to commodity price cycles without durable pricing power.
